How Uber makes
money on a ride

lines.text: Uber says it kept 21% of rider payments worldwide in Q3 2025. A 2026 study of three US drivers' trips says over 50%.
lines.say: Uber says it kept twenty-one percent. A study says over half.

lines.text: First, the size: in 2025, riders and eaters booked $193 billion on Uber, and Uber recorded $52 billion in revenue.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, users booked a hundred ninety-three billion dollars on Uber; its revenue was fifty-two billion.

lines.text: The rider pays an upfront fare. The driver gets a separate upfront offer. Uber keeps the gap, and pays insurance from it.
lines.say: The rider pays an upfront fare. The driver gets a separate upfront offer. Uber keeps the gap, and pays insurance from it.

lines.text: Uber says its take, after insurance and other costs, was 21% worldwide in Q3 2025. A study by Columbia's Len Sherman with GigU, using three US drivers' trips, says the gap topped 50%.
lines.say: Uber says its take, after insurance and other costs, was twenty-one percent worldwide in the third quarter of twenty twenty-five. A Columbia professor's study of three US drivers' trips says it topped fifty percent.

lines.text: The study points to upfront fares for drivers, rolled out in the US in 2022.
lines.say: The study points to upfront fares for drivers, rolled out in twenty twenty-two.

lines.text: Hypothetical $25 ride: at Uber's 21% (after insurance), Uber keeps $5.25. A 50% gap is $12.50, before insurance.
lines.say: Take a hypothetical twenty-five dollar ride. At twenty-one percent, Uber keeps five twenty-five. A fifty percent gap is twelve fifty, before insurance.

lines.text: Either way, rides are Uber's profit engine: Mobility adjusted EBITDA was about $7.9 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Either way, rides are Uber's profit engine. Mobility adjusted EBITDA was about seven point nine billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

post.title: Uber says it keeps 21% of fares. A 3-driver study says 50%+
post.ig:
Uber says it kept 21% of rider payments worldwide in Q3 2025, after insurance. A 2026 study using three US drivers' trips says the gap topped 50%; Uber says the study relies on "a few individual stories."

In 2025, Uber had $193B in gross bookings and $52B in revenue.
Riders pay an upfront fare; drivers get a separate upfront offer; Uber keeps the gap and pays insurance from it. The study (Columbia's Len Sherman with GigU) points to upfront fares for drivers, rolled out in 2022.
Hypothetical $25 ride: $5.25 at 21%, a $12.50 gap at 50% (before insurance).
Mobility adjusted EBITDA: about $7.9B in 2025.

Sources: Uber FY2025 results; Uber; Columbia/GigU study via Fast Company (2026).
News and education, not financial advice.

In 2025 Uber had $193 billion in gross bookings, $52 billion in revenue and about $7.9 billion in Mobility adjusted EBITDA. Sources: Uber FY2025 results, Uber, Fast Company.
